issues.description: Math_unary registration for math.exp2 is outside the class body and breaks the existing decorator chain
issues.detail: In numba/core/typing/mathdecl.py the blank line after the `cases = [...]` list was replaced by `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11): Math_unary = infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)`. Because there is no longer a blank line separating the class from the next `@infer_global(math.atan2)` decorator, and because the conditional registration is placed at module top-level immediately after the class with no separating blank line, the file is hard to read and the indentation/structure is fragile. More importantly, rebinding the module-level name `Math_unary` to the return of `infer_global(...)` (which returns the class) is fine in itself, but doing this *between* the class definition and the next decorated class with no whitespace is a literate-programming failure and an off-by-one in the source layout that future contributors will trip over. State the invariant in a comment: 'register Math_unary as the typing for math.exp2 on Python >= 3.11'.

issues.description: `sys` is imported in mathdecl.py but `sys.version_info` is referenced in mathimpl.py files without importing sys
issues.detail: numba/cpython/mathimpl.py and numba/np/math/mathimpl.py both add `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11): exp2_impl = unary_math_intr(math.exp2, 'llvm.exp2')` but the diff shows no `import sys` added to either file. If `sys` is not already imported at module top, this is a NameError at import time on every Python version. The author has not stated, or verified, the invariant 'sys is in scope here.' This is exactly the class of bug Knuth warns about: proved correct in the author's head, not tried.

issues.description: Version gate is the wrong abstraction; numba already exposes PYVERSION
issues.detail: The test file correctly uses `from numba.core.utils import PYVERSION` and gates with `PYVERSION >= (3, 11)`. The production code in mathdecl.py and the two mathimpl.py files uses raw `sys.version_info >= (3, 11)` instead. Pick one canonical predicate (PYVERSION) and use it everywhere; mixing the two is a readability and consistency defect, and it means a future Python-version bump has to be audited in two idioms. Data-structure-of-the-source-file argument: the project has chosen PYVERSION as the single source of truth for version branching, and this PR should respect that.

issues.description: Test inputs include integer types but math.exp2 in CPython returns float; check that the unsigned-int cases actually exercise what the typing template promises
issues.detail: Math_unary's `cases` list contains int8..int64, uint8..uint64, float32, float64 -> float64 (and float32->float32). math.exp2 in CPython accepts ints and floats and returns float. The test feeds values `[-2, -1, -2, 2, 1, 2, .1, .2]` against `uint16, uint32, uint64` — passing negative values like -2 through a uint type is the test author relying on Python/numpy wraparound semantics. State the invariant: 'for uint types, -2 becomes (2**N - 2), and math.exp2 of that huge value overflows to inf in both CPython and the compiled path, so the comparison is inf == inf.' If that is the intended invariant, write it down; if not, the test is asserting an accident. The existing test_exp does the same thing, so this PR is consistent with prior art — but consistency with an under-audited pattern is not the same as correctness.

issues.description: Release note file is missing a trailing newline
issues.detail: docs/upcoming_changes/10276.new_feature.rst ends with `\ No newline at end of file`. Trivial, but POSIX text files end with a newline; many lint/CI tools will flag this. Also the underline `------------------------------` is exactly 30 chars vs a 28-char title — RST underlines must be at least as long as the title (this one is, so it parses), but a literate-programming reviewer notes that the convention in this directory is presumably consistent and worth matching.

issues.description: No literate comment explains *why* exp2 is version-gated
issues.detail: The reader of this code three years from now will see `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` with no comment and have to go look up that `math.exp2` was added to the Python stdlib in 3.11. One line of comment — `# math.exp2 was added in Python 3.11` — at each of the three gate sites turns a puzzle into a fact. This is the canonical literate-programming missed opportunity: the code is correct (modulo the sys-import issue), but the *explanation* is missing.

issues.description: Complexity and correctness invariant of llvm.exp2 lowering is unstated but worth a one-line audit
issues.detail: `unary_math_intr(math.exp2, 'llvm.exp2')` delegates to LLVM's exp2 intrinsic, which is O(1) per element with hardware-dependent constants and accuracy comparable to libm's exp2. The PR inherits all of the test coverage and accuracy assumptions of the surrounding exp/log/log2 intrinsic lowerings, which is the right move. Worth stating once in the PR description (not necessarily in code): 'exp2 follows the same lowering pattern as exp/log2/log10; accuracy and complexity are inherited from llvm.exp2.' This is a literate-programming note, not a code change.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED and NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT. The algorithmic content is trivial — register math.exp2 with the existing Math_unary typing template and lower it to llvm.exp2, which is the same one-line pattern already used for exp, log, log2, log10. The complexity and correctness story is inherited cleanly from the surrounding intrinsics, so RIGOROUS on that axis. However, two real defects: (1) the two mathimpl.py files reference `sys.version_info` but the diff does not show `import sys` being added — if sys is not already imported, this is an immediate NameError at module load on every Python version, and the author appears not to have run the modified files on Python <3.11; (2) the project already exposes `numba.core.utils.PYVERSION` and the test file uses it, but the production code uses raw `sys.version_info`, splitting the version-branching idiom. Minor literate-programming nits: no comment explaining the 3.11 gate, release-note file missing trailing newline, and the test reuses test_exp's pattern of feeding negative values through uint types without stating the inf==inf invariant that makes the assertion pass. Fix the sys import, switch to PYVERSION everywhere, add one-line "added in Python 3.11" comments at the three gate sites, and this is ready.
